title: Unrestricted perfect charts for one universal direct-image rank condition
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation. Let $E,F$ be finite locally free modules on $X$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Use derived categories of the scheme module categories and their open over-sites in one universe [def-pc-derived-category]. For every $s\in S$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U$, a perfect object $K$ on $U$ [def-pc-perfect-complex], $b\in\mathbf Z$, and $r\in\mathbf N$ such that $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every module $M$ when $i<0$ or $b<i$ [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. For every $g:T\to U$, the single-rank predicate $R_1(f,E,F,g\circ\iota_U)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-single-rank-match] holds if and only if, for every $h:T'\to T$, $H^0(L(g\circ h)^*K)$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. This statement constructs the local complex and comparison, not a representing subscheme. No structure-sheaf unit or connected-fibre hypothesis is imposed; on empty and mixed-fibre neighbourhoods the complex may be the actual zero complex, with rank zero and rank one respectively.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary local normal-form theorem. It gives a neighbourhood U and either a rank r whose universal ordinary direct-image freeness is exactly the reference-rank predicate, or a predicate equivalent to emptiness of the test scheme.

In the fixed-rank case refine U to an affine neighbourhood V of s and apply the existing proper flat affine Cech perfect-model theorem to F. Its bounded nonnegative complex D has perfect Q(D). Affine-local flatness implies tensor flatness and bounded-above flatness implies K-flatness. The bifunctor/single-complex isomorphism and zero terms outside the bounds prove the required tensor-cohomology vanishing.

The derived-pullback counit is invertible on D, by its defining universal property. Compose the quotient comparison, homological-complex pullback comparison, Cech cohomology comparison, degree-zero right-derived pushforward comparison and uniqueness-of-left-adjoint tensor/pullback isomorphisms. This identifies all pulled-back H^0 sheaves with the ordinary direct images. Rewrite the neighbourhood inclusion composite and transfer rank-r freeness along these isomorphisms in both directions.

In the emptiness case use the zero derived object, b=0 and r=1. Zero is perfect via the zero complex on each open. The zero complex is bounded, flat and K-flat, and has zero tensor cohomology in every degree. Derived pullback is additive by its triangulated structure, so it and homology preserve zero. Every module on an empty scheme has every rank, as witnessed by an empty cover. Conversely, a zero module of rank one on a scheme forces that scheme empty: at a point its stalk would have both finrank zero and one. Apply the universal rank condition to the identity test to obtain emptiness.
